bib.title: Contextual Agentic Memory is a Memo, Not True Memory

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Contextual Agentic Memory is a Memo, Not True Memory", Binyan Xu, Xilin Dai, Kehuan Zhang (CUHK / Zhejiang Univ.). Preprint, arXiv:2604.27707v2 [cs.AI], 5 Aug 2026. It is a position paper with a theory result and no new experiments.

COVERAGE: All 19 pages read (72,752 chars): body, references (skimmed for origins), and Appendices A-E. No gaps. The extraction is clean. No embedded instructions found. I did not extract figures; the paper has none that I saw, only Table 1 and Table 2.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: Most agent memory (MemGPT, RAG, Reflexion, Voyager) changes only the context C. It never changes the generator's persistent adaptive state theta, so it is a "memo" and not learning.
  number: none
  setup: conceptual lens. Two paths: change theta (pre-training, fine-tuning, RL, adapters) or change C (prompting, RAG, MCP, skill files, scratchpads).
  quote: "Representative episodic systems (MemGPT, RAG, Reflexion, V oyager) primarily changeC, not the generator's persistent adaptive state."
  where: p.3 (section 2)
- Claim: Frozen State invariant. For agents that only do context engineering, theta_t = theta_0 across sessions. Assisted performance can improve, but competence without the stored trace does not.
  number: theta_t = theta_0
  quote: "for agents that operate exclusively via C-engineering, θt =θ 0 across sessions. The memory-augmented system may improve substantially; what does not change is competence when the acquired trace or rule is not supplied."
  where: p.5, section 3.3
- Claim (Theorem 1, conditional): when the frozen contextual system keeps a positive held-out error margin, retrieval needs Omega(k^2) stored compositional examples. A parametric learner with complexity d needs about d, independent of k. The ratio is Omega(k^2/d), which is Omega(k) for d=O(k) and Omega(k^2) for d=O(1).
  number: n_R >= ((1-δ-ᾱ)/(1-ᾱ))·C(k,2) = Ω(k²); n_R/n_P = Ω(k²/d)
  setup: k base concepts, composition operator, N=C(k,2) pairs. Both systems see the same n examples. Needs Assumption 1: frozen model accuracy with K demonstrations is at most ᾱ<1 on held-out pairs, with δ<1-ᾱ. The parametric learner must be realizable in a class H of VC/Natarajan dimension d. If contextual accuracy reaches the target, the theorem abstains. Proof in App. B.
  quote: "For structured operators with d=O(k) , the ratio is Ω(k); for operators with d=O(1) (e.g. parameterized group operations), it is Ω(k2)."
  where: p.4, section 3.2; proof p.16-17
- Claim: Scope of the theorem. Larger K, better retrieval or in-context rule induction can raise ᾱ and make the bound non-binding. Context length alone does not change the finite bound while a margin remains.
  number: none
  quote: "once contextual accuracy reaches the target 1−δ , the lower bound is non-binding. If a positive margin remains, changing the context-window size alone does not alter the finite bound."
  where: p.5, Remark 2
- Claim: The proof is a coverage argument. Stored pairs are answered correctly. Novel pairs are answered at accuracy at most ᾱ. So CGC <= n/N + (1-n/N)ᾱ.
  quote: "CGC(MR, D)≤n/N+ (1−n/N) ¯α ; solving for CGC≥1−δ yields the Ω(k2) bound on nR."
  where: p.4
- Claim: The constructive example is modular arithmetic, ⊕(a_i,a_j)=(a_i·a_j+c) mod p. It has VC dimension 1, and one labelled example identifies c. The paper says this is an existence proof, not a naturalistic benchmark.
  number: d=1, n_P=O(1/δ), n_R=Ω(k²)
  setup: p prime, k<=p, "frozen LLMs achieve low accuracy on modular arithmetic" is asserted, not measured.
  quote: "A single labeled example (ai, aj, y)determinesc= (y−a iaj) modp, so the VC dimension ofHisd= 1."
  where: p.18, App. E.1
- Claim: Persistent writes turn a one-session prompt injection into a cross-session one ("evil1 to evil2"). Cited attack numbers: MINJA 98.2% injection success; PoisonedRAG 90% attack success with five texts per query against a knowledge base of millions of entries. InjecAgent covers 30 agents and found memory-writing agents more vulnerable.
  number: 98.2%; 90%; 5 texts; 30 agents
  setup: figures come from other papers (Dong et al. 2026; Zou et al. 2024; Zhan et al. 2024), not run by these authors.
  quote: "MINJA [Dong et al., 2026] achieved a 98.2% injection success rate with injected instructions persisting across sessions at minimal utility cost; PoisonedRAG [Zou et al., 2024] shows that five adversarial texts per targeted query achieve 90% attack success against a knowledge base of millions of entries"
  where: p.6, section 3.4
- Claim: Compromise accumulation. P(at least one persistent poisoned write by t) = 1-(1-p_w)^N(t), which tends to 1 for fixed p_w>0. This is stylized: independent trials, no detection or deletion.
  number: 1-(1-p_w)^N(t)
  quote: "the probability of at least one persistent poisoned write by time t is 1−(1−p w)N(t) , which approaches one for fixed pw >0 ."
  where: p.6
- Claim: Attack-path asymmetry, not a safety ranking. Retrieval stores are inspectable and deletable. Poisoned consolidation into weights is harder to inspect and unlearn and has a bigger blast radius.
  number: none
  quote: "The proposition therefore identifies different reachability conditions, not a universal safety ranking between substrates."
  where: p.6
- Claim: Evidence cited for parametric over external reflective memory. Yao et al. 2026 (ParamMem) found parametric storage beats external storage, with the gap growing on held-out question types. Other comparisons (Ovadia 2024, Yang 2026, Mosbach 2023) are task-dependent with no universal winner.
  number: none
  quote: "parametric storage outperforms external storage, with the gapgrowingon tasks requiring transfer to held-out question types"
  where: p.5
- Claim: Effective context saturates well below nominal context (cited from Paulsen 2026). Mechanistic work (Yao 2024, Ye 2025) says standard SFT mostly changes attention routing, not knowledge units.
  number: ≈20k tokens (128k windows); 90% of SFT updates
  setup: cited from other work, not tested here.
  quote: "Paulsen [2026] show effective context utilization saturates at ≈20k tokens even for 128k-context models."
  quote2: "Ye et al. [2025] quantify this: 90% of SFT parameter updates contribute nothing to knowledge enhancement."
  where: p.7 and p.5
- Claim: MemGPT's own team concedes raw appending is weak. Their proposed fix, sleep-time compute, rewrites context tokens, not weights, so the paper says it is still a "well-organized novice".
  number: none
  quote: "The MemGPT team acknowledge that “simply appending raw experience is a poor approximation of learning” and propose “sleep-time compute” as a remedy [Packer, 2025]—but their consolidation rewrites context tokens, not weights."
  where: p.6
- Claim: Recommended hybrid design, based on Complementary Learning Systems. Scoped, deletable episodic retrieval stays the operating substrate. A separate asynchronous consolidation channel (LoRA, MEMIT, TTT, self-distillation) adds provenance, versioned checkpoints and regression guards. Raw, user-specific, temporary information stays in retrieval, and durable updates go into rollback-able scope-specific adapters.
  number: none
  quote: "The consolidation pipeline therefore requires trace provenance (so the origin of every distilled experience is auditable), versioned checkpoints (so any bad consolidation can be rolled back), and regression guards (so consolidation is blocked when utility, retention, or adversarial metrics degrade)."
  where: p.8
- Claim: Proposed benchmark metric, Compositional Generalization over Time (CGT). Expose the agent to concepts only in isolation for T sessions. Then test novel combinations in four arms (episodic retrieval, retrieved-rule summaries, consolidation, hybrid), with the acquired trace withheld and compute matched. Current memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMem) measure recall, not learning.
  number: T sessions, 4 arms
  quote: "The performance hypothesis is falsified in a domain if a fixed-state contextual system consistently matches an updateable system on held-out compositions under this matched budget."
  where: p.8-9
- Claim: Memory taxonomy (Table 1). Working = context window, session only. Episodic = external store, cross-session, exemplar-based. Semantic = weights, pre-training. Experiential = adaptive state, updated by FT/CL/TTT, learned transfer. The paper says deployed agents mostly occupy the episodic row.
  where: p.2

LIMITS (authors' own, section 7)
- No compute-matched frontier-model experiment demonstrates the Frozen Novice effect, and existing empirical comparisons are task-dependent.
- Reliable large-scale consolidation is not shown. Forgetting, recency bias, contamination, interference, unlearning, reproducibility and certification remain barriers.
- The separation is conditional on measured ᾱ. It is not a ranking of ICL against fine-tuning. In domains where in-context induction reaches the target, retrieval may be enough.
- The security analysis compares attack paths, not absolute safety.
- App. C admits an earlier Fano-based margin claim was too strong. A uniform margin needs a packing/separation condition, so ᾱ must be measured empirically.
- Quote: "We do not provide a compute-matched frontier-model experiment demonstrating the Frozen Novice effect, and existing empirical comparisons are task-dependent."
- Dated or weak points: the theorem assumes uniform sampling of pairs and a realizable hypothesis class. The domain examples (clinical, legal, engineering) are asserted, not measured. The attack numbers belong to other papers. Several citations are 2026 preprints that I did not check.
- A reviewer should treat this as an opinionated position paper, not an empirical result.

BUILDS ON: Packer et al. 2024 (MemGPT); Park et al. 2023 (Generative Agents); Shinn et al. 2023 (Reflexion); Wang et al. 2023 (Voyager); McClelland et al. 1995 and O'Reilly et al. 2014 (Complementary Learning Systems); Chi et al. 1981 (novice vs expert); Lewis et al. 2021 (RAG); Meng et al. 2022/2023 (ROME/MEMIT); Zhang et al. 2026b (experience compression spectrum); Hu et al. 2026 (Memory in the Age of AI Agents); Yao et al. 2026 (ParamMem); Vapnik 1998 (learning bound); Greshake et al. 2023 (prompt injection); Dong et al. 2026 (MINJA); Zou et al. 2024 (PoisonedRAG); Lampinen et al. 2025 (latent learning); Memento (Zhou 2025); Packer 2025 (Letta sleep-time/continual learning in token space). The paper also cites Mem0 (Chhikara 2025), MemOS (Li 2025), A-MEM and MemoryBank as continuing the same retrieval paradigm.

CODE: none. The only snippet worth keeping is a phrase: "the agent is permanently doing .predict(C), never .train()" (p.6).

FIGURES: none. Table 1 (p.2) is the memory taxonomy and Table 2 (p.18) lists continual learning methods (full FT, LoRA, EWC, SSR, ROME/MEMIT, TTT). Table 2 columns are parameter cost, data required and scale.

PROBLEMS: None serious. The extraction has a few spacing and symbol glitches ("V oyager", "Assumption 3.2" where the text means Assumption 1). The paper's Theorem 1 is cited in text as "Assumption 3.2". Many references are dated 2026 (the paper itself is Aug 2026), so check any citation before reuse. The note's source list already includes arXiv 2505.22101 (MemOS) and 2310.08560 (MemGPT), both of which this paper cites. I did not read the note beyond its front matter. Relevance: it sharpens the note's MemGPT/OS framing with a critique (memory as context, not weights) and the security point (auto-written memory is a persistence path for injection).
